fields.why: SVI quartiles (four groups) each get an RR against Q1 with Fisher tests, and hotspot incidence is compared across SVI quartiles.

Reading each SVI theme by its content (minority/English as race and nativity, household composition/disability as disability and age) is defensible. So is recording every SVI theme as SES, since the brief lists area indexes under SES.

The quartile RRs vs Q1 and the highest-vs-other-quartiles incidence test are per-group vs referent. The three urbanicity strata only set RRs side by side, with no test across them; the Fisher tests are within strata, so the mechanical flag is a false hit.

brief_issues: The brief does not say whether the subthemes of an area index (SVI) are recorded as SES or under the SPD each one measures.
